steps.what: Translate application needs into electronics design constraints and architecture choices
Design electronic components, software or systems and resolve technical trade-offs

tasks.design: Retain application interpretation and design decisions with the engineer using {OTHER}, the existing electronics design environment. Existing libraries and calculations support the work; the digest does not establish that a generated design can replace the engineer's trade-off work across these applications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Design choices depend on physical behaviour, interfaces and application-specific constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing design tools already assist representation and calculation; no new saving is established for the core design judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete requirements, component interactions and behaviour outside simplified models.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a defensible architecture and recognising assumptions that need physical verification.
tasks.altitude: Core design responsibility and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain electronics interface and design trade-offs

evidence.claim: Application-specific electronics design remains engineering judgement; existing automated calculations do not establish incremental labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary is design reasoning and its design artefact, excluding separate software-operation effort, project review and physical testing. A roll-up assigns overlapping tool work once.

The customer and system requirements owner supply existing application/interface requirements before s1. The engineer clarifies and records constraints in s1 before designing in s2; no complete structured requirements feed is assumed.
Missing or conflicting requirements require human clarification and engineering analysis. No generated safety or design-adequacy flag is introduced.
Test native design functions before custom tools; existing solver and library runtime earn no saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because the design process is unchanged.
unknowns: Existing design environment and work mix
research_questions: Which distinct repeated tool actions remain after existing native automation, without counting core design judgement as removed?

already_counted.description: Requirements interpretation and electronics design remain fully counted

incremental.description: No changed tool or process to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains actual electronics design judgement and excludes existing automated calculations from human savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Set up the engineering model and specify checked parameter cases for the software
Operate the software through repeated specified parameter cases and collect the results
Check model behaviour, convergence and physical meaning and revise the engineering analysis

tasks.design: Configure native batch or parameter-sweep functions in {OTHER}, the electronics engineering analysis application, for cases the engineer has explicitly specified. The engineer retains setup and interpretation; failed runs stop for review, and solver runtime is excluded from labour savings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some analysis workflows still repeat parameter entry, run initiation and result collection by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing analysis applications may support native batch execution of explicit cases.
tasks.still_hard: Correct models, component assumptions, convergence and whether numerical output represents physical behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Rejecting executable but physically misleading analysis.
tasks.altitude: The engineer may repeat fewer interface actions while retaining all model and interpretation decisions.

reach.task: Prepare a reproducible analysis run record
reach.learn: Parameter units, model versions and result provenance

evidence.claim: Native batch execution of explicitly specified electronics analysis cases is plausible; actual application support and labour savings need local testing.
The digest's FEABench example distinguishes executable simulation calls from correctness, supporting physical-meaning checks rather than treating successful execution as validation.

assumptions: Boundary is operating an analysis application, excluding design choices, physical testing and formal project adequacy review. Overlapping tool effort in the broad design task is assigned once.

The engineer produces the run specification in s1, including model/version, component-data version, parameter names, units, explicit case values, boundary conditions, solver settings, requested outputs and output locations. All capture and setup time remains counted in s1.

S2 executes only the supplied cases and records status and provenance. Missing units, unsupported settings, failed runs or convergence warnings stop the affected batch and require manual operation/review; no model invents a simulation setup.
The application produces run results after execution in s2 before s3. Interpretation and model correction remain fully counted in s3; computing time was never human labour.

Test native batch configuration before custom scripts. If native sweeps already run today, new saving is zero. Allow 6 focal hours per 100 baseline for configuration upkeep, batch failures and sampled manual comparisons.
unknowns: Native batch capability and current usage
research_questions: Does native batch execution save hands-on actions after run-specification capture and full engineering interpretation?

already_counted.description: Model setup and explicit run-case capture remain counted
Physical-meaning checks and analysis revision remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain batch configuration and resolve failed runs and sample comparisons

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85; gross saving 15 less 6 upkeep gives net 9. Range 1-5 assumes manual repeated parameter/run/collection actions remain; setup, interpretation and failed-case review remain, while solver runtime earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Evaluate project work for effectiveness, technical adequacy and compatibility of the proposed solution

tasks.design: Retain technical adequacy and compatibility evaluation with the engineer using evidence in {DOCS} and {OTHER}, the engineering analysis environment. Native checks can supply evidence, but their successful completion does not determine overall adequacy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complex interactions and missing evidence are not exhausted by a finite checklist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing engineering tools support evidence review without establishing a new saving in the judgement itself.
tasks.still_hard: Unmodelled interactions, conflicting evidence and assurance that matches the intended use.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which evidence is insufficient and requiring further work.
tasks.altitude: The engineer retains technical assessment responsibility and decision rights.

reach.task: Explain cross-interface adequacy concerns to a project lead

evidence.claim: Technical adequacy evaluation remains contextual engineering judgement rather than a deterministic pass based only on completed checks.

assumptions: Boundary is evaluation of existing project work, excluding producing designs, running analyses and executing corrective work.

Project designers and test/analysis owners produce their existing evidence before review. The engineer selects evidence, checks versions and records limitations within the fully retained evaluation time; no structured adequacy flag is assumed.
OTHER means the existing engineering analysis environment. Missing or contradictory evidence requires manual investigation or further tests, not a generated approval.
Native review and requirements tools are the first option for a separately established evidence-administration need.
Zero incremental upkeep because the evaluation process is unchanged.
unknowns: Assurance requirements and engineer's approval remit
research_questions: Which adequacy concerns cannot be settled by existing formal checks and need additional engineering evidence?

already_counted.description: Evidence review and technical assessment remain fully counted

incremental.description: No new system or procedure to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Exact technical assessment, requirement and evidence versions, stated limitations and required actions; changed evidence or conclusions require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains substantive technical evaluation without inventing a removable reporting baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine technical priorities and responsibilities for electronics equipment activities
Direct or coordinate manufacture, installation, maintenance, operation or modification and resolve technical issues

tasks.design: Keep technical direction and issue coordination with the engineer. Existing work records in {PROJECT} can support discussions, but no new reporting baseline or automated equipment action is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work direction depends on technical readiness, people and conditions during execution.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes that coordination.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, unexpected equipment behaviour and determining when work must stop or escalate.
tasks.human_edge: Making accountable technical decisions and coordinating the people who carry them out.
tasks.altitude: The engineer's coordination role and technical authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate an engineering concern into an agreed work priority
reach.learn: Execution constraints and technical change-control boundaries

evidence.claim: Technical direction and coordination remain human decisions and conversations in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is the engineer's direction and coordination, excluding manufacturing or maintenance execution by other roles, design creation and separate project review.

The project or equipment owner supplies existing work needs before s1. Execution teams produce progress and issues after directions in s1 and during s2; their unchanged work is not claimed as saved or newly transferred.
No structured readiness flag or automatic work allocation is assumed. Unclear progress requires direct clarification, fully counted in s2.
Test existing project records before custom tools for separately demonstrated administration; no build is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because coordination practice is unchanged.
research_questions: Is there a material separate reporting workload, beyond actual technical direction, that could be improved?

already_counted.description: Technical direction and coordination remain fully counted

incremental.description: No changed system or procedure to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains technical priorities and execution coordination rather than treating human or physical work as removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native batch operation may reduce repeated interface actions; design, evidence interpretation, adequacy review and technical direction remain engineering work.
reach: Explain electronics interface trade-offs to systems engineers
Coordinate technical priorities with equipment work leads
role.ambitious_version: Make repeated analysis operations more reproducible while preserving the engineering judgement that determines whether a design or result is useful.
